answer: To resist sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind voting weight to a delayed, work-linked bond. An identity mints influence only after publishing a unique computational receipt and locking a ferrous reserve that is slashed if peers later prove the receipt clones another trail. New accounts wait through a cooling window, so a sudden gale of fabricated identities cannot vote in the same epoch they appear. Attesters treat each confirmed unique trail as a pearl of weight that vests slowly; mass-produced accounts therefore pay real capital and time for almost no early voting power.
